author: Rahul kp
title: Merger vs Purchase
simple_words: If all five AS 14 conditions are met it is a merger. If even one fails, it is a purchase.

definitions.meaning: Pooling of interests: all assets and liabilities pass over, and shareholders of the transferor continue as shareholders of the transferee.
Any amalgamation that fails even one merger condition. The transferee in effect buys the business of the transferor.

key_points: Merger needs all assets and liabilities of the transferor to be taken over
==90%== of transferor equity shareholders (face value) become transferee shareholders
Consideration is paid in equity shares; cash only for fractional shares
!!Merger: no adjustment to book values!!, and the business is meant to continue

rows: Not preserved; statutory ones via AAR

insight.text: Meeting four of five conditions still makes it a purchase.

memory_trick.explanation: Merger: the whole family (assets, liabilities, 90% holders) moves into one house, nothing re-priced. Purchase: you shop for the business and pay a price.

steps: Check all assets and liabilities taken
Check consideration is in equity shares
Check business continues, no book value change
exam_tip: Name the type first. Then apply the pooling or purchase method to reserves and the difference.

doubt.question: Is paying some cash allowed in a merger?
doubt.answer: Only for fractional shares. Any other cash makes the consideration fail the test, so it becomes a purchase.

mistakes.wrong: Treating 75% shareholder acceptance as enough for a merger
mistakes.right: AS 14 asks for at least 90% of equity shareholders (by face value), excluding shares held by transferee.
In a merger the difference is adjusted in reserves, not shown as goodwill or capital reserve.

mistakes.wrong: Cancelling transferor reserves in a merger
mistakes.right: In a merger the transferor's reserves are generally carried to the transferee's books with the same identity.

Checker 1: Key point 4, step 4 and the memory trick ('nothing re-priced') say there is no adjustment to book values. AS 14 condition (v) does allow adjustments made only to ensure uniform accounting policies. Correct version: 'The business of the transferor is intended to be continued, and no adjustment is made to book values except to ensure uniformity of accounting policies.'

Checker 1: Mistake 1 'right' line: the 90% test excludes shares already held by the transferee or its subsidiaries or their nominees, not only shares held by the transferee. Correct version: 'Holders of at least 90% of the face value of equity shares of the transferor, other than shares already held by the transferee, its subsidiaries or their nominees, must become equity shareholders of the transferee.'
Checker 1: Table row 5 (Merger): better to say 'Existing carrying amounts (adjusted only for uniform accounting policies)', so it matches AS 14 and the corrected key point 4.
